terms.meaning: the language that describes how page elements look, such as colour and size.
a label added to HTML elements so a style rule can target them.
the part of a style rule that says which elements it applies to.
adapting the layout to different screen widths.
layout methods that arrange items in rows, columns or grids.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Resetting default spacing
sections.what: Removes default margins and padding and makes all sizes include borders, so layouts behave predictably.
sections.why: Likely reason: browsers add different default spacing, and this makes them consistent.
sections.watch_out: Any element that relied on default spacing will look tighter.

sections.name: body
sections.title: Page background
sections.what: Sets a purple gradient background filling the whole screen with dark text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely a visual choice.
sections.watch_out: Low contrast could affect readability if the colours change.

sections.name: .container
sections.title: Main content box
sections.what: Puts the content in a centred white panel with rounded corners and a shadow, up to a set maximum width.
sections.why: Likely reason: frames the tool as a card on the coloured background.
sections.watch_out: Content wider than the maximum width is hidden where overflow is cut off.

sections.name: header
sections.title: Header area
sections.what: Gives the top banner the same purple gradient with white centred text and generous padding.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely branding.

sections.name: header h1
sections.title: Main heading size
sections.what: Sets the page title to a large size with some space below.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Smaller screens are handled separately in the narrow-screen block.

sections.name: header p
sections.title: Subtitle text
sections.what: Makes the header subtitle slightly large and a bit faded.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .tabs
sections.title: Tab bar layout
sections.what: Places the tab buttons in a row on a light grey strip that can scroll sideways if needed.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets all five tabs fit or scroll on narrow screens.
sections.watch_out: Scrolling hides tabs off screen, which some users may miss.

sections.name: .tab-button
sections.title: Tab button look
sections.what: Styles each tab button with padding, no border, a transparent background, grey text and a hidden underline.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely a clean tab look.
sections.watch_out: The hidden underline is what the active state later colours.

sections.name: .tab-button:hover
sections.title: Tab hover effect
sections.what: Gives a tab a light grey background and darker text when the mouse is over it.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the user which tab they are pointing at.

sections.name: .tab-button.active
sections.title: Active tab look
sections.what: Makes the selected tab purple, white in the background, with a purple underline.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows which tab is open. This matches the active class added by app.js.
sections.watch_out: Renaming the active class breaks this highlight.

sections.name: .tab-content
sections.title: Tab content area
sections.what: Hides each tab's content by default and adds padding and a short fade-in animation.
sections.why: Likely reason: only one tab is shown at a time.
sections.watch_out: The fade animation runs every time the tab is shown.

sections.name: .tab-content.active
sections.title: Showing the active tab and fade animation
sections.what: Shows the selected tab's content and defines the fade-in animation that slides it up slightly.
sections.why: Likely reason: pairs with the hide rule above so exactly one tab is visible.

sections.name: .tab-content h2
sections.title: Tab heading style
sections.what: Colours the tab's heading purple and sets its size.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .tab-content > p
sections.title: Tab description style
sections.what: Makes the paragraph under each tab heading grey with spacing below.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .form-group
sections.title: Form field spacing
sections.what: Adds space below each form field group.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .form-group label
sections.title: Form labels and inputs
sections.what: Makes labels bold, grey and placed above their inputs, and styles text and number boxes.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes forms readable.
sections.watch_out: Some input types are styled through a shared list continued below.

sections.name: .form-group textarea
sections.title: Text area styling
sections.what: Makes text areas full width with padding, a thick grey border and rounded corners.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .form-group textarea:focus
sections.title: Focused field highlight
sections.what: Changes the border to purple when a text area is selected and removes the default outline.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows which field is active.
sections.watch_out: The default outline is removed, so keyboard users rely on this colour change to see focus.

sections.name: .btn-secondary
sections.title: Secondary button look
sections.what: Gives secondary buttons padding, rounded corners, bold text and a pointer cursor.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A second rule for the same class later overrides some of these values.

sections.name: .btn-primary
sections.title: Primary button look
sections.what: Gives main action buttons a purple gradient with white text.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the main action stand out.

sections.name: .btn-primary:hover
sections.title: Primary button hover
sections.what: Lifts the primary button slightly and adds a glow when hovered.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives feedback that the button is clickable.

sections.name: .btn-primary:disabled
sections.title: Disabled primary button
sections.what: Fades and disables the click cursor for primary buttons that are not available.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows that an action cannot be used right now. No code here disables buttons, so the rule may be unused.
sections.watch_out: Nothing in the visible code adds the disabled state, so it may do nothing.

sections.name: .btn-secondary
sections.title: Secondary button outline
sections.what: Gives secondary buttons a white background, purple text and a purple border with a small top margin.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: This rule repeats and overrides the earlier secondary button look.

sections.name: .btn-secondary:hover
sections.title: Secondary button hover
sections.what: Fills a secondary button with purple and turns its text white on hover.
sections.why: Likely reason: clear hover feedback.

sections.name: .result-box
sections.title: Result panel
sections.what: Puts results in a light grey panel with a purple left edge and rounded corners.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets results apart from the form.

sections.name: .result-box h3
sections.title: Result panel heading
sections.what: Colours result headings purple with space below.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: #validatorOutput
sections.title: Planner, author and validator output
sections.what: Gives the output areas a white background, padding, a limit on height with scrolling, and spacing.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps long answers from pushing the page down.
sections.watch_out: Long answers scroll inside the box, which can hide content.

sections.name: .question-card
sections.title: Question card
sections.what: Gives each question a white box with a purple left edge.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes each question stand out.

sections.name: .question-card h4
sections.title: Question card heading
sections.what: Colours the question heading dark grey with space below.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .question-meta
sections.title: Question tag row
sections.what: Places question badges side by side with gaps and space above.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps type and category tags neat.

sections.name: .badge
sections.title: Badge shape
sections.what: Makes badges small rounded pills with bold text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .badge-type
sections.title: Type badge colours
sections.what: Colours type badges pale blue with dark blue text.
sections.why: Likely reason: distinguishes question types.

sections.name: .badge-category
sections.title: Category badge colours
sections.what: Colours category badges pale purple with dark purple text.
sections.why: Likely reason: distinguishes categories from types.

sections.name: .filters
sections.title: Filter row layout
sections.what: Places the model filter dropdowns and refresh button in a wrapping row with spacing.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps filters usable on small screens.

sections.name: .filters select
sections.title: Filter dropdown look
sections.what: Styles filter dropdowns with padding, a grey border, rounded corners and larger text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .models-grid
sections.title: Model card grid
sections.what: Arranges model cards in a grid that fits as many columns as the width allows, at least 280 pixels each.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps model cards evenly laid out.

sections.name: .model-card
sections.title: Model card box
sections.what: Gives model cards a white box with a grey border, rounded corners and padding.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .model-card:hover
sections.title: Model card hover
sections.what: Lifts a model card, adds a shadow and purple border when hovered.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows which model the pointer is on.

sections.name: .model-card h4
sections.title: Model name heading
sections.what: Colours the model name dark grey with a slightly larger size.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .model-card .model-meta
sections.title: Model details section
sections.what: Adds space above, a divider line, and padding to the model details block.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates details from the name and tags.

sections.name: .model-meta-item
sections.title: Model detail row
sections.what: Places each detail label and value on one line, pushed apart, with small spacing.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes a neat two-column list.

sections.name: .model-meta-item .label
sections.title: Detail label colour
sections.what: Makes detail labels grey.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .model-meta-item .value
sections.title: Detail value colour
sections.what: Makes detail values bold and dark grey.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .quality-score
sections.title: Quality score pill
sections.what: Shows the quality score as a small rounded pill with bold text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .quality-high
sections.title: High quality colour
sections.what: Colours high quality scores green.
sections.why: Likely reason: signals a strong model at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The threshold for this colour is set in app.js, so both must agree.

sections.name: .quality-medium
sections.title: Medium quality colour
sections.what: Colours medium quality scores yellow.
sections.why: Likely reason: signals a middling model.

sections.name: footer
sections.title: Footer look
sections.what: Gives the footer a light grey background, padding, centred text and a top border.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .status-badge
sections.title: Status badge shape
sections.what: Makes the backend status badge a small rounded pill with bold text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .status-online
sections.title: Online status colour
sections.what: Colours the online status green.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows a healthy backend.

sections.name: .status-offline
sections.title: Offline status colour
sections.what: Colours the offline status red.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows a problem.

sections.name: footer a
sections.title: Footer link look
sections.what: Colours footer links purple with no underline.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: footer a:hover
sections.title: Footer link hover
sections.what: Underlines a footer link on hover.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the link is clickable.

sections.name: .loading-overlay
sections.title: Full-screen loading overlay
sections.what: Covers the whole screen with a dark see-through layer and centres its content on top of everything.
sections.why: Likely reason: blocks clicks while a request runs.
sections.watch_out: The overlay is hidden by a style set in index.html, so both must stay in agreement.

sections.name: .loading-overlay p
sections.title: Loading message text
sections.what: Makes the loading message white, larger and spaced below the spinner.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .spinner
sections.title: Spinning loader
sections.what: Draws a round ring that spins continuously while work is in progress.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows that the app is busy.

sections.name: .error-message
sections.title: Error message box
sections.what: Shows errors in a pink box with dark red text and a red left edge.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes problems obvious.

sections.name: .success-message
sections.title: Success message box
sections.what: Shows success messages in a green box with dark green text.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the error style but with positive colours.

sections.name: .validation-section
sections.title: Validation section spacing
sections.what: Adds space below each group of validation results.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .validation-section h4
sections.title: Validation section heading
sections.what: Colours validation group headings dark grey with spacing below.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .validation-item
sections.title: Validation item box
sections.what: Gives each validation line a white box with a green left edge.
sections.why: Likely reason: a green edge marks a passing item by default.
sections.watch_out: Items are green unless another class changes the colour.

sections.name: .validation-item.error
sections.title: Failed validation item
sections.what: Changes the left edge of a validation item to red.
sections.why: Likely reason: flags a problem.

sections.name: .validation-item.warning
sections.title: Warning validation item
sections.what: Changes the left edge of a validation item to yellow.
sections.why: Likely reason: flags a item worth a look.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 768px)
sections.title: Narrow screen layout
sections.what: On screens 768 pixels wide or less, reduces padding, shrinks the heading, lets tabs wrap into two per row, and shows model cards in one column.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the layout usable on phones.
sections.watch_out: Tab sizing here overrides the desktop tab rule, so changes must be made in both places.

sections.name: pre
sections.title: Code and raw data display
sections.what: Shows raw answers in a dark box with light text, padding and sideways scrolling.
sections.why: Likely reason: raw answers are displayed as code when the expected format is missing.

sections.name: code
sections.title: Code font
sections.what: Sets code text to a standard monospaced font.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

summary: The stylesheet that sets the colours, spacing, layout, tabs, cards, buttons, model grid, status badges and mobile layout for the frontend.
purpose: Makes the classic page look consistent and usable on phones and desktops.
why: Likely reason: keeps visual rules in one file separate from the page structure. Reason for specific values is not stated in the code.
how: Rules are read top to bottom. Global resets come first, then layout pieces, then components such as tabs, forms, buttons and cards, then status colours, the loading overlay, messages, and finally a narrow-screen block and code display styles.
inputs: Class names and ids added by index.html and app.js.
risks: Some selectors are grouped with others that are not shown in this packet, so changes may affect more elements than expected. Colours carry meaning such as green for good and red for poor.
debug: If an element looks wrong, search the file for its class name. If the mobile layout breaks, check the rules inside the narrow-screen block.
